question: Can we do option A for us to still build the API as part of this project? Or the API kind of have to come with the remote MCP?

No. They aren't coupled. Sept 25 bundled them because they shared a server, one retrieval service in `apps/website` with two adapters, not because either needed the other. You can keep Option A and a local MCP, and still build the API in this project.

## A correction to my case for dropping it

I gave two reasons. One was wrong.

- **Wrong:** "under A its credential would be a full-write space token, held by a server." A hosted API doesn't need to hold anything. The client keeps the bundle, refreshes it itself, and sends a short-lived access token as `Authorization: Bearer` on each request. The server forwards that token to Supabase, so row-level security runs as the space account. The token passes through the server but is never stored. All the custody in Sept 25 came from the agent-principal design: stored login secrets, the grant table, provisioned auth users. Option A removes all of that.
- **Overstated:** "it means building the hosted service local was chosen to avoid." Most of Sept 25's hosting cost was that credential machinery plus the credential-URL release gate. Without them, the API is a few thin routes. The Nov 10 reasons for going local (later write-back, and scientists already working in agentic harnesses) don't argue against a hosted read API either.

## Three ways to build the API under A

| | What it is | Cost | Catch |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. The RPCs are the API** | Document the narrow retrieval RPCs. A developer calls them over Supabase's built-in HTTP layer (PostgREST) using the bundle. | No new hosting | The database schema becomes a public contract, errors arrive as raw Postgres errors, and search makes the developer embed the query first through the unauthenticated route. |
| **2. Thin hosted API** | The `/api/v1/...` routes from Decision 8 in `apps/website`, authenticated by the bearer token and calling the same RPCs. | A few routes | Parity with the MCP has to be kept across two code paths. |
| **3. Option 2, with the MCP calling the API** | The local MCP sends its tool calls to the hosted API instead of to Supabase. | Same as option 2 | The MCP stops working if the website is down. |

I'd recommend **option 3**:

- **It fixes the embedding problem.** Search would take a query string, check the bearer token, and embed on the server, so neither the MCP nor a developer touches the open route. That resolves the second risk I raised last turn instead of just recording it.
- **Parity comes for free.** There's one code path, so the API-parity requirement holds by construction rather than by testing.
- **No new kind of dependency.** The MCP already needs the network to reach Supabase and the embedding route.

In effect, option 3 brings back Sept 25's "one retrieval service, two adapters", minus the two things Nov 10 rejected: the remote MCP and the agent principal.

## What keeping it changes in the drafted revisions

- `headless-retrieval-api` **stays**. Its three requirements survive with "agent credential" reworded to "the space account's access token". The subagent's earlier finding still applies: this spec assumes a hosted server, which is exactly what this keeps.
- `discourse-mcp` keeps its parity requirement, reworded.
- Decision 1: the API stays in `apps/website` and the MCP is local. Decision 8 keeps its endpoint table. Decision 6 goes back to embedding on the server, with authentication added.
- One new risk: under A, the bearer token is a full-write credential travelling through the website. Decision 8 already keeps credentials out of logs. That rule now has to cover the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs too.

What it doesn't bring back is ChatGPT. That needs a remote MCP, which Nov 10 dropped.

Agreed. The name and the text both say the *credential* is read-only. "It MUST NOT authorize modification … even when its principal has write permissions" describes A2 or B. Under A it's false: the credential can write, and only the tools stop it.

My draft fix didn't solve this either. I split it into "Credential scope" in `agent-read-access` and a separate "Read-only tool surface" in `discourse-mcp`. Someone reading either spec alone would get half the picture: one says the credential can write, the other says there are no write tools, and neither says the second is the only thing standing in for the first.

So here it is as one requirement, with the mechanism in its name:

> ### Requirement: Read-only is enforced by the MCP's tools, not the credential
>
> The handed-over session SHALL carry the space account's full permissions, including write. Read-only access SHALL come only from the MCP's tool surface: the MCP SHALL expose retrieval tools and no tool that creates, modifies or deletes nodes, relationships, sharing permissions or sessions. The database SHALL NOT be relied on to refuse writes made with the session. Missing, expired or signed-out sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.
>
> #### Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node
> - **GIVEN** the space account can edit a node
> - **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify that node
> - **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification
> - **AND** the node remains unchanged
>
> #### Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools (accepted v0 limitation)
> - **GIVEN** a process holds the handed-over session
> - **WHEN** it modifies a node by calling the database directly with that session
> - **THEN** the database permits the modification
> - **AND** this is accepted under Option A; database enforcement is Option A2
>
> #### Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval
> - **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing, expired or signed-out session
> - **THEN** no discourse data is returned

How the specs change:

- It **replaces** "Read-only shared credential" in `agent-read-access`. That's where the access rules live, and anyone asking "can the agent write?" will look there first.
- The separate `discourse-mcp` "Read-only tool surface" requirement I proposed is **dropped**. That spec's "Four retrieval tools" requirement already points to the `agent-read-access` contract, so there's no duplicate rule to drift.
- The two scenarios together state the contract: you can't write through the MCP, but you can by going around it. The second one is the line A2 would flip.

If you keep the API as option 3, one wording change follows: "the MCP's tools" becomes "the MCP's tools and the API's routes", since the API is a second surface that must expose nothing that writes.

one does 2 adapters mean?

An **adapter** is a thin layer that translates one kind of incoming request into a call to shared code, then translates the answer back. It contains no retrieval logic of its own.

In the Sept 25 design, all the logic sat once in a **retrieval core**: four functions (get node, search, list types, get context) that query the database and apply every rule about what's readable, ranking, limits and errors. The two adapters sat in front of it, each speaking a different protocol:

```
HTTP request  ──► API adapter ──┐
                                ├──► retrieval core ──► database
MCP tool call ──► MCP adapter ──┘
```

Take one operation through both:

- **API adapter.** It receives `GET /api/v1/nodes/123` with a bearer token, checks the input, calls `getNode("123")`, and turns the result into an HTTP response: JSON with status 200, or 404 `not_found`.
- **MCP adapter.** It receives a `get_node` tool call with `{id: "123"}`, checks the input, calls the same `getNode("123")`, and turns the result into an MCP tool result, or an MCP tool error with the same `not_found` code.

That's why Sept 25 could promise parity: both paths go through one function, so they can't drift apart. It's also why that doc said not to have the MCP call the public API over HTTP. Both adapters lived in the same server, so the MCP could call the core directly.

## Under a local MCP

I said option 3 "brings back one service, two adapters". That was loose. Here's what each option actually looks like:

- **Option 2 — two adapters, in two places.** The API adapter on the website and the local MCP on the user's machine each call the database RPCs directly. The RPCs act as the shared core, but query embedding and error mapping have to be written twice, once in each adapter. That's where the two can drift.
- **Option 3 — one adapter, plus a client in front of it.** The core and the API adapter live on the website. The local MCP translates MCP tool calls into HTTP calls to that API:

  ```
  MCP tool call ──► local MCP ──HTTP──► API adapter ──► retrieval core ──► database
  ```

  Strictly, that's one adapter, not two: the local MCP is a client of the API rather than a second adapter beside it. Parity holds anyway, and more simply than in Sept 25, because every request goes through the same API. Embedding and errors live in one place.

So "two adapters" is the right name for Sept 25 and for option 2. Option 3 is a single API with the MCP as one of its clients.
but the local MCP calling supabase directly is ok too. why we need the adapter?

You don't need it. A local MCP calling Supabase directly is fine, and it's what my drafted revisions already assume: Decision 1 has the MCP "talking straight to Supabase". Strictly, the MCP is still an adapter, because it turns MCP tool calls into RPC calls. What you're asking is whether a hosted layer belongs between it and the database. For the MCP alone, it doesn't.

I recommended option 3 mostly for two reasons. Neither holds up:

- **Query embedding.** True, the MCP can't embed a search query itself and has to call the website's unauthenticated route. But the fix is to add a bearer-token check to that one existing route, which is a few lines. A whole API layer isn't needed for that.
- **Parity.** That only matters if a direct API exists. Without one, there's nothing to keep in step with.

It doesn't buy any security under A either. In option 3 the MCP still holds the full-write bundle so it can send tokens to the API. A layer in the middle doesn't change what the MCP could do with that bundle.

Going direct has two costs, and both are manageable:

1. **Search still goes through the website**, for embedding. So "direct to Supabase" really means Supabase plus that one route. It belongs in the plan as a dependency, and authenticating the route can be part of this change or a small follow-up.
2. **The RPCs become a contract with every installed copy of the MCP.** It's a local package on users' machines that you can't force-update. If you rename an RPC or change its arguments, older copies break. A hosted API would absorb that, which is the one real thing it buys. For a pilot cohort, keeping RPC signatures stable (or adding new versions alongside old ones) handles it.

That makes the API a separate question: **do you want a developer-facing HTTP API in v0, for people not using MCP?** It's a product decision, not something the MCP needs. And if the MCP calls the RPCs directly, option 1 (document the RPCs as the API) costs almost nothing, since the MCP already proves they can be called from outside. Its drawbacks are the ones I listed before: the schema becomes a public contract, errors come back as raw Postgres errors, and developers have to embed the query themselves.
ok, so update the spec with these decisions

Writing the revisions. One assumption I'm making: I'm **keeping the direct API**, since you asked whether you could still build it, and recording its shape (documented RPCs vs thin hosted routes) as open. The spec requirements read the same either way, so only the design has to choose.

# Proposal

<!-- Ported from the 2026-09-25 shared OpenSpec session in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_).
     Revised 2026-11-12 for the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: local MCP, Option A. -->

## Why

Users need to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent interface without opening Roam or Obsidian during retrieval or installing a platform-specific MCP for each. This v0 makes that collection available through a local MCP and a documented direct API, using a space account session handed over by the plugin.

## What Changes

- Provide four read-only operations through both interfaces: get a node, search nodes, discover node types, and get discourse context. The MCP is local: users install it, and the agent client launches it on their machine. Validate setup and these operations in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is not supported in v0.
- The plugin hands the agent its own session for the space account, as specified in `mcp-session-access`. The agent acts as the space (Option A): the session carries the space account's full permissions, and read-only is enforced by the MCP's tools and the API's operations exposing only retrieval, not by the database.
- Retrieve every synced discourse node readable by the space account, including accessible shared nodes that have never been imported into the client. Permissions follow current access: new access becomes available and removed access stops working. Signing out a handed-over session stops it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds stay valid until they expire.
- Use per-space sessions as the v0 identity model. Access to another space's synced but unpublished nodes requires a bundle from that space. This does not promise one credential representing a person's combined access across spaces.
- Return node ID, title, type, full synced text body, and source/provenance link when fetching a node. Attachment downloads and image/file contents are excluded.
- Reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. V0 does not require title-only re-embedding. Hybrid search, including keyword indexing and reciprocal rank fusion, is deferred to a later release. Return node ID, title, type, short excerpt, and source/provenance link, ordered by relevance.
- Default search to 10 results, allow at most 30, and omit pagination. Apply no relevance cutoff in v0: weak matches may be returned. Empty results mean no eligible searchable nodes under the access and filter constraints, not a judgment that nothing is relevant.
- Discover types present on currently readable nodes. Accept an optional filter of one or more type IDs, matching any selected type; omission searches all types. Further search-scope toggles and filters are deferred.
- Return discourse context as incoming and outgoing one-hop explicit discourse relationships, including relationship type/direction and connected-node ID, title, and type. Return only relationships with two readable endpoints; retrieve connected bodies separately. Ordinary backlinks are excluded.

### Boundaries and known limitations

- Retrieval reads already-synced data. Candidate-node ingestion/retrieval, general non-discourse content, canvas functions, write-back, relation creation, candidate elevation, feedback capture, arbitrary-depth server traversal, and imported-only filtering are outside v0. Agents may repeat one-hop calls.
- Accessible but unimported results may feel unfamiliar or outside the user's working collection. Results must not imply local import membership. Tracking that membership is not a v0 dependency. Semantic coverage follows the existing embedding inputs, which differ by platform and node representation; information absent from those inputs does not directly contribute to matching. Real-query evaluation examples and relevance thresholds are deferred.
- Database-enforced read-only access (Option A2), a separate agent principal (Option B), a hosted MCP, and ChatGPT support are outside v0.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `agent-read-access`: Plugin-initiated session handoff, the space account as principal and its current read access, and read-only enforcement by the MCP's tools and the API's operations.
- `discourse-retrieval`: Node payloads, semantic search using existing embeddings, readable-type discovery/filtering, and authorized one-hop discourse context.
- `headless-retrieval-api`: Documented direct access to the four operations using the space account session and shared retrieval/access rules.
- `discourse-mcp`: Local MCP delivery of the same operations, validated in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex.

### Modified Capabilities

- None; the repository currently has no existing OpenSpec capability specs.

## Impact

Expected affected areas are the narrow retrieval RPCs and integration with existing semantic search in `packages/database`, a new local MCP package, the connect command in `apps/roam` and `apps/obsidian` (through `mcp-session-access`), and `apps/website` as the host of the query embedding route and possibly the direct API. This change depends on `mcp-session-access`, specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff` and not yet in this repository. Read-only is enforced by the interfaces, not the database, so ENG-2057's feasibility evaluation of read-only delegation is not used by v0. The separate agent-access experiment is a design input, not evidence of deployed behavior or approval of its broader storage-read scope.

### Open decisions and dependencies

- **All hands (resolved 2026-11-10):** a local MCP, and Option A for agent identity. The per-space baseline stands; whether one agent should span several spaces is open.
- **Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 notes record option A2; the spec owner chose A on 2026-11-12. See design.md, Decision 4.
- **Design:** Credential-bearing MCP URLs are removed. The direct API's shape is open (design.md, Decision 1). Existing embeddings are retained; the retrieval query must add access/type filtering and limits without the existing semantic function's relevance threshold. No broader read-auditing project is implied.
- **Validation:** Requirements and scenarios are captured in the capability specs. Implementation tasks and a small real-query relevance evaluation set remain to be developed; no numerical relevance or latency target has been agreed.
- Scope reflects the supplied September 15 meeting research brief, the 2026-09-25 exploration, and the 2026-11-10 decisions. Historical July aspirations do not expand v0.

doc = f"""# Design

<!-- Ported from the 2026-09-25 shared OpenSpec session in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_).
     Revised 2026-11-12 for the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: local MCP, Option A. -->

## Context

See proposal.md for motivation and the four capability specs for the behavior contract. This design follows the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: a local MCP, and Option A for agent identity (see Decision 4). It depends on the `mcp-session-access` handoff specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff`, which is not yet in this repository.

The checkout has useful pieces, but no implemented agent-grant layer was found:

{ctx}
- `apps/website/app/api/embeddings/openai/small/route.ts` embeds text with the team's OpenAI key. It has no authentication: it applies CORS only, which non-browser callers ignore.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** Reuse existing data, vectors, and access semantics; expose only read operations to agents; keep the MCP and the direct API on the same retrieval semantics; expose sync gaps without silently substituting incomplete content.

**Non-Goals:** A new personal identity system, copied permission snapshots, a second embedding pipeline, hybrid ranking, attachment/storage APIs, or a general-purpose database proxy. Database-enforced read-only access (Option A2), a separate agent principal (Option B), and a hosted MCP are out of v0. The database package owns SQL/contracts; the local MCP owns its transport.

## Decisions

### 1. A local MCP that calls the database directly

The MCP is a local stdio server that the user installs and the agent client launches on the user's machine. It connects to Supabase with the handed-over space account session and calls the narrow retrieval RPCs directly. No DG-hosted layer sits between the MCP and the database, and no DG-hosted MCP endpoint exists in v0.

```
Roam / Obsidian --> connect command --> session bundle (shown once)
                                               |
                                 local MCP config on the user's machine
                                               |
agent client --stdio--> local MCP --+--> Supabase retrieval RPCs (as the space account)
                                    |
                                    +--> website embedding route (search queries only)
```

The retrieval RPCs are the shared core. Each MCP tool validates its inputs, calls one RPC, and returns structured results plus a compact text representation. All tools are marked read-only.

The RPCs are a contract with every installed copy of the MCP, and those copies cannot be force-updated. Change an RPC's signature only by adding a new version alongside the old one.

**Direct API (shape open).** A developer-facing API for callers not using MCP stays in scope (`headless-retrieval-api`). Its shape is not decided: (a) document the retrieval RPCs themselves as the API, callable through Supabase's HTTP layer with a bundle — no new hosting, but the schema becomes a public contract, errors arrive as raw Postgres errors, and callers must embed search queries themselves; or (b) thin routes in `apps/website` that authenticate the bearer access token and call the same RPCs. The MCP depends on neither.

**Alternatives:** A hosted remote MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 design) reaches ChatGPT and needs no install, but requires a hosted credential transport. It was rejected on 2026-11-10 in favour of a local MCP, given the constraint to write to the platform later and target users who already work in agentic harnesses. Routing the local MCP through a hosted API was also considered: it would absorb RPC changes, but adds no security under Option A, because the MCP still holds the bundle.

### 2. Hand the MCP its own space account session

The credential is a Supabase session for the space account, opened by the plugin and handed over as a bundle: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and refresh token. `mcp-session-access` specifies the handoff, the session registry, and sign-out. The plugin keeps no copy and shows the bundle once. The MCP persists each rotated refresh token and runs as a single instance per bundle.

**Alternative (superseded 2026-11-10):** The 2026-09-25 design provisioned a separate Supabase auth user per agent grant, issued an opaque final credential through a website management session, and stored the agent's login secret server-side. That needs a hosted server and a separate principal, and Option A has neither.

### 3. ~~Proposed MCP connection uses a credential-bearing URL~~ — removed

Removed 2026-11-10. It existed to carry a credential to a hosted MCP through clients that cannot send custom headers. A local MCP reads the bundle from its own configuration. The client/redaction release gate and the OAuth alternative are removed with it.

### 4. Read-only is enforced by the MCP's tools and the API's operations, not the credential (Option A)

Decided 2026-11-10: the MCP acts as the space account. The handed-over session carries the space account's full permissions, including write. The database does not refuse writes made with it. Read-only is a property of the interfaces: the MCP exposes only the four retrieval tools and no tool that creates, modifies or deletes data, and the direct API exposes no such operation either.

Retrieval RPCs run as the space account under its existing row-level security, so reads follow the space's current access with no grant layer.

**Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product notes record "option A2" (Roam block `guIcK3Z9M`), which adds read-only enforcement at the database session level. The spec owner chose plain A on 2026-11-12. Confirm which was agreed before implementation.

**What A does not protect against:** any process that obtains the bundle can write to the space — edit nodes, call sync/upsert functions, or call `create_secret_token` to open a website management session. The 2026-11-10 notes name the threat as unaligned agentic harnesses that bypass flimsy guards; a tool-layer gate is that kind of guard.

**Alternatives:** (A2) add database session-level read-only on top of A, about four more days of work. (B) a separate, permanently read-only agent principal with an `agent_reader` role and a grant table — the 2026-09-25 version of this decision. The 2026-11-10 notes record B as adding substantial complexity for marginal or no security gain (per MAP).

{d5}

### 6. Reuse semantic vectors with a retrieval-specific query

Embed each search query with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions to match the existing table. A local MCP has no server and no provider key, so it embeds through the existing website route `/api/embeddings/openai/small` and passes the vector to the search RPC. That route is unauthenticated today; see Risks. A caller-supplied vector cannot widen access, because the RPC ranks only nodes readable by the caller.

{d6rest}

{d7}

### 8. Tool contract and operational behavior

The MCP tools and their inputs:

| MCP tool | Inputs |
| --- | --- |
| `get_node` | Node ID |
| `search_nodes` | Query, optional type IDs, optional limit |
| `get_node_types` | None |
| `get_discourse_context` | Node ID |

The direct API exposes the same four operations with the same inputs, whichever shape Decision 1 settles on.

Use shared Zod input/output schemas and generate or check the tool and API documentation against them. Reject blank queries, malformed IDs, empty explicitly supplied type filters, and non-integer/out-of-range limits with `invalid_request`. Omitted limits default to 10; valid limits are 1-30. Unknown but syntactically valid type IDs simply match no nodes. Results carry a request ID and `data` or an error object with a stable code and safe message.

Missing, expired, or signed-out sessions fail authentication. Use the same `not_found` for nonexistent and unreadable nodes, `content_unavailable` for a readable node with missing required synced content, and `result_too_large` for response-budget failures; database and embedding failures are dependency errors. Return these as MCP tool errors with the same codes rather than serializing exceptions; a hosted API maps them to 401, 404, 409, 422 and 503. Do not turn failed queries into successful empty collections.

Keep diagnostic logs to request ID, operation, duration, result count, and error category. Exclude the bundle, refresh and access tokens, query text, node bodies, and provider payloads. A local MCP's logs stay on the user's machine. No read-history UI or auditing subsystem is added. Documentation includes the install and setup flow, private bundle handling, search coverage/limits, sync-gap errors, and source-link limitations.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The bundle grants write, and read-only rests on the interfaces] → Accepted under Option A (Decision 4). The MCP and the API expose no write operation, and a test asserts it. Adopting A2 is the upgrade path.
- [The bundle is a full-write credential in a plain file the agent harness can read] → Agent clients keep MCP configuration in plain files on the user's machine (for example `claude_desktop_config.json`, or `~/.claude.json` for Claude Code), and an agent harness with file access can read them. Accepted for v0 under Option A. Setup documentation states the risk.
- [Cutting off one MCP depends on `mcp-session-access` sign-out] → If per-session sign-out is not in v0 (open there as task 0.4), the only cut-off is changing the space password, which signs out every plugin instance of the space. A signed-out session keeps its current access token until `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
- [The query embedding route is unauthenticated] → Search depends on it, and today anyone can spend the team's OpenAI quota through it, independent of this change. Mitigation: add a bearer-token check to the route, in this change or as a follow-up (undecided).
- [Installed MCP copies pin the RPC signatures] → Copies on users' machines cannot be force-updated. Add RPC versions alongside old ones rather than changing signatures in place.
- [Agent writes are unattributable] → Content tables have no actor column, so a write made with the bundle cannot be told apart from a person's. Out of scope for v0.
- [One bundle reads one space] → A user with several spaces needs one MCP entry per space. Whether one agent should span several spaces is an open product question.
{risks}

## Migration Plan

1. Land `mcp-session-access` first: the session registry, the handoff helper, and the plugin connect command. This change depends on it.
2. Add the narrow retrieval RPCs — node fetch, search without a relevance threshold, type discovery, and one-hop context — through the database's declarative schema/migration workflow. Existing clients and search RPCs retain their behavior.
3. Build the local MCP with the four tools over those RPCs and the embedding route, and the direct API in whichever shape Decision 1 settles on.
4. Test permission gains/losses, both platform payloads, shared unimported nodes, type filters, negative similarities, missing embeddings/content, inaccessible relation endpoints, and parity between the MCP and the direct API. Assert that no write operation is exposed. Install the MCP in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with a test space's bundle, record client versions, and demonstrate all four operations with Roam and Obsidian closed. Run required repository validation before requesting implementation review.
5. Release the MCP to a limited validation cohort, then expand only after those checks pass. No bulk content migration or re-embedding is part of rollout.
6. Rollback withdraws the MCP package and signs out registered MCP sessions; without per-session sign-out, change the space password. Additive retrieval RPCs can remain unused; do not delete synced nodes, content, vectors, or existing group access.

## Open Questions

The credential label copy, example queries for documentation, and a future relevance evaluation dataset can be settled during implementation without changing this architecture.

### Per-capability open decisions

<!-- Held here rather than in the spec deltas: openspec validate warns that a
     "## Open decisions" section in a delta is not carried into the main spec on archive. -->

- **`agent-read-access`:** The per-space model stands as the v0 baseline after the 2026-11-10 decision. Whether one agent should span several spaces is open.
- **`discourse-mcp`:** The client set is Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is out of v0.
- **`discourse-retrieval`:** Implementation design for access/type filtering, limits, excerpts, errors, and missing embeddings is above. Real-query relevance examples and numerical quality targets are deferred. Hybrid search is future work.
- **`headless-retrieval-api`:** The API's shape is open (Decision 1). No latency target or broader read-auditing capability is committed.
"""
pathlib.Path('design.md').write_text(doc)
print("design.md written,", doc.count("\n### "), "decision/sub headings")
PY

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Let a space hand an agent its own session for the space account, so the agent reads the space's synced discourse graph with the space's current access.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Session handoff from the plugin

An agent SHALL obtain its credential through the `mcp-session-access` handoff: a Roam or Obsidian plugin signed in as the space account opens a new session and shows the user a bundle once. No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required.

#### Scenario: Setup from either supported platform

- **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in an authenticated Roam or Obsidian client
- **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new session of that client's space account
- **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged

### Requirement: Per-space principal

The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection and SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts used by the same human. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space.

#### Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes

- **GIVEN** a human uses spaces A and B and a node in B is not readable by A's space account
- **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A
- **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B
- **AND** access through B requires a bundle from space B

#### Scenario: Accessible shared node

- **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing
- **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node
- **THEN** the node is eligible without requiring local import or authorship by the space account

### Requirement: Current permissions and revocation

The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions. Removing access SHALL stop subsequent retrieval of affected data, and adding access SHALL make affected synced data eligible, without a new bundle. Signing out a handed-over session SHALL stop it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds MAY remain valid until they expire.

#### Scenario: Permissions change after handoff

- **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over
- **THEN** subsequent requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B
- **AND** a new bundle is not required

#### Scenario: Session sign-out

- **WHEN** a user signs out a handed-over session
- **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh that session
- **AND** requests fail once its current access token expires

### Requirement: Read-only is enforced by the MCP's tools and the API's operations, not the credential

The handed-over session SHALL carry the space account's full permissions, including write. Read-only access SHALL come only from the interfaces: the MCP SHALL expose retrieval tools and no tool that creates, modifies or deletes nodes, relationships, sharing permissions or sessions, and the direct API SHALL expose no such operation. The database SHALL NOT be relied on to refuse writes made with the session. Missing, expired or signed-out sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.

#### Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node

- **GIVEN** the space account can edit a node
- **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify that node
- **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification
- **AND** the node remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools (accepted v0 limitation)

- **GIVEN** a process holds the handed-over session
- **WHEN** it modifies a node by calling the database directly with that session
- **THEN** the database permits the modification
- **AND** this is accepted under Option A; database enforcement is Option A2

#### Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval

- **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing, expired or signed-out session
- **THEN** no discourse data is returned

## Purpose

Expose headless discourse retrieval to agent clients through one platform-independent local MCP, run on the user's machine with a space account session handed over by the plugin.

### Requirement: Four retrieval tools

MCP SHALL expose tools for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types, and get-discourse-context. INSTRUCTION:
Create the task list that breaks down the implementation work.

Before writing tasks, check design.md for Open Questions. If any of them
would change what gets built, resolve them with the user first - do not
bake an unstated assumption into the task list.

**IMPORTANT: Follow the template below for tracked tasks.** The apply phase parses
checkbox format to track progress. A box holding only `x` counts as done,
upper or lower case and with any spacing, so `- [ x]` is done too. Every
other marker, including `- [~]`, `- [-]` and an empty `- []`, reads as
unfinished. A line with no checkbox is not tracked at all.

Guidelines:
- Group related tracked tasks under ## numbered headings
- Each tracked task MUST be a checkbox: `- [ ] X.Y Task description`
- Tasks should be small enough to complete in one session
- Order tasks by dependency (what must be done first?)
- Track implementation and verification work that can be completed before
  archive. If the requested workflow includes archive or work that requires
  this change to be archived, preserve those steps as plain bullets in an
  optional `## Workflow follow-up` section at the end of tasks.md. These
  bullets are reference information outside tracked task progress.
- Each task MUST state how to verify completion (a test, command,
  observable behavior, or delivered artifact). Put the verification in
  that task's checkbox description. Use a separate verification task only
  when it checks broader integration or system behavior that spans
  multiple implementation tasks.
- Each task group MUST land the tests and documentation its own work
  calls for. Do NOT collect testing or documentation into a final group -
  when a late group first exercises work from an early one, the failures
  cascade back through every group in between and force rework. A group
  whose work calls for neither, such as scaffolding or dependency setup,
  carries neither. A final group is for integration checks only, not for
  the tests and docs an earlier group owed.

The spec is updated for your decisions, and `openspec validate headless-mcp-retrieval` passes.

## What changed

All six artifacts were revised. 16 requirements and 31 scenarios remain.

- **`design.md`**
  - Decision 1 is now *a local MCP that calls the database directly*, with the direct API's shape marked open.
  - Decision 2 is now *the plugin hands the MCP its own space account session*.
  - Decision 3 is left as a struck-through "removed" entry, so the numbering doesn't shift.
  - Decision 4 is now *read-only is enforced by the MCP's tools and the API's operations, not the credential*. It records that the meeting notes say A2 and you chose A.
  - Decision 6 now has the MCP embed queries through the website route.
  - Decision 8 is now a tool contract rather than an HTTP contract.
  - Risks, Migration and Goals are rewritten. Decisions 5 and 7 are unchanged, apart from the client list in 7.
- **`agent-read-access`** gets the requirement in the wording you reviewed: one place, mechanism in the title, and a scenario stating that a write made outside the tools succeeds.
- **`discourse-mcp`** — clients are Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, with ChatGPT explicitly out. Parity is reworded around the shared session.
- **`discourse-retrieval`** — one phrase changed. **`headless-retrieval-api`** — five credential phrases changed. Its requirements fit either API shape, so neither had to wait on that decision.
- **`proposal.md`** — Why, What Changes 1–4, Boundaries, Capabilities, Impact and Open decisions.

I searched for leftover terms (pseudo-user, agent credential, credential URL, grants, ChatGPT). Every remaining hit is deliberate: a superseded alternative, the removed Decision 3, or an explicit "not supported".

`tasks.md` doesn't exist yet. `openspec instructions tasks --change headless-mcp-retrieval --json` gives its template.

## Turning the spec into tickets

OpenSpec has no concept of a ticket. Its unit of work is **`tasks.md`**:

- Checkboxes written as `- [ ] 2.1 …`, grouped under `## 2.` headings and ordered by dependency.
- Each task says how it's verified.
- Each group delivers its own tests and docs; a final group may only hold integration checks.
- `/opsx:apply` works through the boxes and ticks them, and `/opsx:archive` merges the specs into `openspec/specs/` once everything is done.

Tickets sit on top of that:

1. **One task group = one Linear ticket.** The rule that each group delivers its own tests and docs makes each group a self-contained, reviewable PR, which is what a ticket needs. Your token handoff spec in Roam already does this: its Tasks section says "the groups are the proposed ticket boundaries".
2. **Give each group a `Carries:` line** naming the requirements and decisions it implements. That's the traceability link: ticket → requirement → scenarios. The scenarios become the ticket's Done When, and `scope-check` later compares the PR against that.
3. **Create each ticket with `dg-create-engineering-ticket`.** Repo rules say agent-created tickets start in `Ticket Draft` with the `Created by Claude` label, and you review them before they move on. They go in the existing Linear project for this work (P-DIS-186).
4. **The change folder lasts across several PRs.** Each ticket's PR ticks its own boxes in `tasks.md`, and the archive happens only when the last group lands.

Three things to know before writing `tasks.md`:

- **Its own instructions say to resolve open questions that change what gets built first.** The direct API's shape is one, since hosted routes add a whole group of tasks. Whether to authenticate the embedding route in this change is another.
- **`mcp-session-access` should be its own change**, ported from the token handoff spec, with its own tasks and tickets. This change depends on it, and Migration step 1 already says so.
- **The Linear milestones assume the old design.** M1 is "Safe read access to database", which presumed read-only enforced by the database. Under Option A that isn't built, so the milestone needs renaming before tickets are attached to it.

- [proposal.md](openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/proposal.md): why, what changes, capabilities, impact
- [design.md](openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/design.md): the 8 decisions, risks, migration plan
- [specs/agent-read-access/spec.md](openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/specs/agent-read-access/spec.md)

- [specs/headless-retrieval-api/spec.md](openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/specs/headless-retrieval-api/spec.md)

The folder isn't committed yet, so it only exists in your local checkout. `openspec show headless-mcp-retrieval` also prints it in the terminal.

## What "thin hosted routes" changed

`openspec validate` still passes, and nothing still says the API's shape is open.

- **Decision 1:** the API is a set of thin routes in `apps/website`. Each route checks the caller's bearer token against Supabase, embeds search queries on the server, and calls the same retrieval RPCs as the space account, so row-level security applies. The routes keep no credential between requests. Documenting the RPCs directly as the API is recorded as the rejected alternative, and the diagram now shows the developer → API path.
- **Decision 8** has its original title and endpoint column back: the four `/api/v1/...` routes alongside their MCP tools. Error codes map to 401/404/409/422/503 on the API side.
- **New risk:** under Option A, the bearer token sent to the API can write. The API never stores it, and log redaction has to cover the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs, not just application logs.
- **Embedding:** this choice fixes it for API callers, because API search embeds on the server behind authentication. MCP search still depends on the unauthenticated route, so that risk stays, now scoped to the MCP.
- **Proposal Impact:** `apps/website` now hosts the API routes for certain, rather than "possibly".

The specs didn't change. The `headless-retrieval-api` requirements already worked with either shape.

One decision still affects what goes into `tasks.md`: whether adding auth to the embedding route is part of this change or a follow-up. If it's in this change, its task likely shares code with the API's search route, since both need the same bearer check.

- # Proposal
  - ## Why
    - Users need to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent interface without opening Roam or Obsidian during retrieval or installing a platform-specific MCP for each. This v0 makes that collection available through a local MCP and a documented direct API, using a space account session handed over by the plugin.
  - ## What Changes
    - Provide four read-only operations through both interfaces: get a node, search nodes, discover node types, and get discourse context. The MCP is local: users install it, and the agent client launches it on their machine. Validate setup and these operations in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is not supported in v0.
    - The plugin hands the agent its own session for the space account, as specified in `mcp-session-access`. The agent acts as the space (Option A): the session carries the space account's full permissions, and read-only is enforced by the MCP's tools and the API's operations exposing only retrieval, not by the database.
    - Retrieve every synced discourse node readable by the space account, including accessible shared nodes that have never been imported into the client. Permissions follow current access: new access becomes available and removed access stops working. Signing out a handed-over session stops it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds stay valid until they expire.
    - Use per-space sessions as the v0 identity model. Access to another space's synced but unpublished nodes requires a bundle from that space. This does not promise one credential representing a person's combined access across spaces.
    - Return node ID, title, type, full synced text body, and source/provenance link when fetching a node. Attachment downloads and image/file contents are excluded.
    - Reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. V0 does not require title-only re-embedding. Hybrid search, including keyword indexing and reciprocal rank fusion, is deferred to a later release. Return node ID, title, type, short excerpt, and source/provenance link, ordered by relevance.
    - Default search to 10 results, allow at most 30, and omit pagination. Apply no relevance cutoff in v0: weak matches may be returned. Empty results mean no eligible searchable nodes under the access and filter constraints, not a judgment that nothing is relevant.
    - Discover types present on currently readable nodes. Accept an optional filter of one or more type IDs, matching any selected type; omission searches all types. Further search-scope toggles and filters are deferred.
    - Return discourse context as incoming and outgoing one-hop explicit discourse relationships, including relationship type/direction and connected-node ID, title, and type. Return only relationships with two readable endpoints; retrieve connected bodies separately. Ordinary backlinks are excluded.
    - ### Boundaries and known limitations
      - Retrieval reads already-synced data. Candidate-node ingestion/retrieval, general non-discourse content, canvas functions, write-back, relation creation, candidate elevation, feedback capture, arbitrary-depth server traversal, and imported-only filtering are outside v0. Agents may repeat one-hop calls.
      - Accessible but unimported results may feel unfamiliar or outside the user's working collection. Results must not imply local import membership. Tracking that membership is not a v0 dependency. Semantic coverage follows the existing embedding inputs, which differ by platform and node representation; information absent from those inputs does not directly contribute to matching. Real-query evaluation examples and relevance thresholds are deferred.
      - Database-enforced read-only access (Option A2), a separate agent principal (Option B), a hosted MCP, and ChatGPT support are outside v0.

      - `headless-retrieval-api`: Documented direct access to the four operations using the space account session and shared retrieval/access rules.

    - ### Modified Capabilities

Read-only is enforced by the interfaces, not the database, so ENG-2057's feasibility evaluation of read-only delegation is not used by v0. The separate agent-access experiment is a design input, not evidence of deployed behavior or approval of its broader storage-read scope.

Existing embeddings are retained; the retrieval query must add access/type filtering and limits without the existing semantic function's relevance threshold. No broader read-auditing project is implied.
      - **Validation:** Requirements and scenarios are captured in the capability specs. Implementation tasks and a small real-query relevance evaluation set remain to be developed; no numerical relevance or latency target has been agreed.

===== proposal.md =====
# Proposal

## Why

The "Architecture Decisions" milestone of [Post-V0 Roam–Obsidian sync architecture][project] holds tickets whose approach was deferred during v0. Deciding them one ticket at a time gave conflicting answers: [ENG-1824] marked the upsert route out of scope, while the 2026-07-17 meeting agreed it would use the route ([ENG-2412]). This change records the milestone's decisions together, working backwards from the tickets that already exist ([ENG-2416]).

## What Changes

- Roam sync and Obsidian sync write each node in one `upsert_concepts` call, with its Content inside the Concept. They switch now and don't wait for the upsert route ([ENG-1823], [ENG-1824], [ENG-1794]).
- Roam sync moves onto the CrossApp converters that Roam publish uses, in small steps under [ENG-2165]: [ENG-2061] first, then [ENG-1824].
- One upsert route in Next.js stays the goal, with no date ([FEE-890]). It accepts the plugin's own Supabase login.
- Discovery returns `CrossAppNode` with the fields it was missing ([ENG-2091]). **BREAKING** for `@repo/database` callers: the `SharedNode` type is removed.
- Obsidian imports relations made elsewhere between its own nodes, the same way Roam does ([ENG-2394]).
- [ENG-1866] closes: the validation it asked for happened in other tickets. [ENG-2166] closes once [ENG-2165] lands.

## Decisions: settled and open

Settled by Sid (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22):

- One upsert route stays the goal. When it gets built isn't decided ([FEE-890]).
- [ENG-1823] and [ENG-1824] don't wait for the upsert route. This departs from the 2026-07-17 agreement.
- No data migration is needed for the single write ([ENG-1823], [ENG-1824]).
- The upsert route's details stay open until someone picks up [FEE-890].
- [ENG-1824] is a step of [ENG-2165], which becomes the parent and is split into small PRs.
- Obsidian looks for relations the way Roam does, on import and refresh ([ENG-2394]).
- Confirmed proposals: the upsert route accepts the plugin's login; [ENG-1794] moves with its children; [ENG-2061] only removes `RoamFullContentNode`; [ENG-2166] closes after [ENG-2165]; [ENG-1986] comes later than [ENG-1823]; the `CrossAppNode` field list (a review of this change found three more fields, in `design.md`); [ENG-1985] builds the node converter; two bug tickets; [ENG-1866] closes; the [ENG-2394] details; the reject-or-look-up question waits for [ENG-1986].

Settled by the tickets or the code:

- Discovery returns `CrossAppNode` and `SharedNode` is removed ([ENG-2091] Solution and Done When). [ENG-2045] follows it.
- [ENG-1986] is no longer blocked by [ENG-1985]: the CrossApp-to-database converters it needs are on main.
- [ENG-2005] and [FEE-891] are built with [FEE-890].
- "sourceId" means `sourceLocalId`, which already maps to `localId` ([ENG-2091]).

Still open:

- Michael: the upsert route's details in [FEE-890] and [FEE-891] (reject or look up a missing relation type, the name, what a user does with an error, who computes embeddings, how the tests run). Michael also reviews the [ENG-2165] split.
- Marc-Antoine: for the three listing fields the first field list missed, add them to `CrossAppNode` or change their callers ([ENG-2091]); the field questions in [ENG-1986].
- Michael: whether refresh-all checks for relations when the user has no imported nodes, in both apps ([ENG-2428], Product Decisions).

`design.md` has one entry per decision. The specs state Sid's answers as requirements; review of this change is where Michael and Marc-Antoine weigh in.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `graph-writes`: how Roam and Obsidian write nodes to the shared database, one write per node, and which converters they use.
- `graph-upsert-route`: the planned Next.js route that takes CrossApp types and writes them to the database.
- `shared-node-discovery`: what discovery returns when a user lists the nodes in a shared space.
- `cross-space-relation-import`: how Roam and Obsidian find and import relations that another space made.

### Modified Capabilities

None. The project has no specs yet.

## Impact

- Roam: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`, `conceptConversion.ts`, `convertRoamNodeToFullContent.ts`, `roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, `DiscourseNodeSuggestiveRules.tsx` (a Content-only write), `refreshAllImportedNodes.ts`, and the 8 files that use `SharedNode`.
- Obsidian: `syncDgNodesToSupabase.ts`, `upsertNodesAsContentWithEmbeddings.ts`, `importNodes.ts`, `importRelations.ts`, `ImportNodesModal.tsx`, `types.ts`.
- `packages/database`: `crossAppContracts.ts`, `lib/sharedNodes.ts`, `lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`.
- Website: a new route under `apps/website/app/api/` when [FEE-890] is built.
- Database: no schema change and no migration.

===== shared-node-discovery =====
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

What Roam and Obsidian receive when they list the nodes in the spaces shared with the user, which is also what node import starts from.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Discovery returns CrossApp nodes

Discovery SHALL return each listed node as a `CrossAppNode`. Roam and Obsidian SHALL still get everything they read from the listing today: the node's space id, space name, space URI and platform; its node type, resolvable to the node type Roam imports it as; its author, resolvable to the name Obsidian shows; and its direct Content's metadata. Sources: [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091).

#### Scenario: Roam lists the nodes in a shared space

- **WHEN** Roam's discover dialog lists the nodes in a shared space
- **THEN** each node is a `CrossAppNode`, and the dialog shows each node's title, space name, space URI and modified time as before ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091))

#### Scenario: Obsidian shows authors

- **WHEN** Obsidian's import modal lists the nodes in a shared space
- **THEN** it shows each node's author name as before ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091), [ENG-2045](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045))

#### Scenario: Obsidian needs the original file path

- **WHEN** Obsidian lists the nodes in a shared space
- **THEN** each node carries its direct Content's metadata, so import can read the file path the node had in its source vault ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091), [ENG-2045](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045))

### Requirement: The listing leaves out full content

Discovery SHALL NOT include a node's full content. A node's modified time SHALL still be the latest time of its Concept, its direct Content and its full Content. Import SHALL fetch the full content of each node it imports. Sources: [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091).

#### Scenario: Listing, then importing

- **WHEN** discovery lists nodes and the user imports one of them
- **THEN** the listing has no full content for any node, and import fetches the full content of the node being imported ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091))

#### Scenario: Only the body changed

- **WHEN** the source edits only a node's body, so only its full Content changes
- **THEN** discovery reports the node's new modified time, and refreshing the imported copy picks up the edit ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091))

### Requirement: Removing SharedNode loses no behavior

`SharedNode` SHALL be removed, and every behavior that used it SHALL keep working: Roam's discover dialog (display and filter), Roam import, refresh and asset import, and Obsidian import. Sources: [ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091), [ENG-2045](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2045).

#### Scenario: Filtering the discover dialog

- **WHEN** a user filters Roam's discover dialog by space name, space URI or title
- **THEN** the dialog shows the same nodes it showed before `SharedNode` was removed ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091))

#### Scenario: Import with a source slot

- **WHEN** a user imports a node whose Source slot points at another node in the same space
- **THEN** the imported node's Source reference resolves the same way it did before `SharedNode` was removed ([ENG-2091](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2091))
===== cross-space-relation-import =====
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

How Roam and Obsidian find relations that another space created and bring them into the graph or vault, including relations between two of the user's own nodes.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Import and refresh find relations between the user's own nodes

On every node import and every refresh, Roam and Obsidian SHALL look for relations in other spaces whose two ends both resolve in the graph or vault, whether each end is an imported node or one of the user's own nodes. Sources: [ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394), [ENG-2340](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2340), [ENG-2339](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2339).

#### Scenario: Another user relates two of my nodes

- **WHEN** user A publishes nodes A and B, user B imports them, relates them and publishes the relation, and user A then runs an import or a refresh in Obsidian
- **THEN** Obsidian imports the relation between A and B ([ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394))

#### Scenario: The same case in Roam

- **WHEN** the same happens, user A has imported at least one node in Roam, and user A runs an import or a refresh
- **THEN** Roam imports the relation between A and B ([ENG-2340](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2340), [ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394))

#### Scenario: Refresh with nothing imported

- **WHEN** user A has imported no nodes and runs "Fetch latest content from imported nodes" in Obsidian
- **THEN** Obsidian still looks for relations between user A's own nodes ([ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394))

#### Scenario: Only one end resolves

- **WHEN** a relation's other end resolves neither to an imported node nor to one of the user's own nodes
- **THEN** the relation is not imported ([ENG-2339](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2339), [ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394))

### Requirement: A relation is imported once

Roam and Obsidian SHALL NOT import a relation whose source, destination and relation type match a relation the graph or vault already holds. Sources: [ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394).

#### Scenario: Refresh twice

- **WHEN** a refresh imports a relation, and the user runs a refresh again
- **THEN** the second refresh doesn't create another copy of that relation ([ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394))

### Requirement: Obsidian tells the user what it imported

When the lookup imports one or more relations, Obsidian SHALL show a notice with the number of relations it imported. Sources: [ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394).

#### Scenario: Two relations found

- **WHEN** an import or a refresh imports two relations
- **THEN** Obsidian shows a notice that says it imported 2 relations ([ENG-2394](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2394))
===== graph-upsert-route =====
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

The planned Next.js route through which Roam and Obsidian write nodes, relations and schemas, so the conversion to database rows runs on the server instead of in each plugin.

Only the settled behavior is specified here. The route's open details (what it does with a missing relation type, its name, what a user can do with an error, who computes embeddings, how its tests run) are in `design.md`, open for Michael.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The route takes CrossApp types and writes them in one upsert

The upsert route SHALL accept any mix of the root CrossApp types (node schemas, relation type schemas, relation triple schemas, nodes and relations) for one space, and SHALL write them in one database upsert. Sources: [FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890), [ENG-2412](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2412).

#### Scenario: A payload of nodes and their schemas

- **WHEN** an action function sends nodes together with their node schemas for one space
- **THEN** the route writes the schemas and the nodes in one database upsert ([FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890))

### Requirement: The route identifies the caller from the plugin's own login

The upsert route SHALL identify the caller from the Supabase session that the plugin signed in with. It SHALL NOT depend on website cookies, which plugin requests from Roam or Obsidian don't carry. Sources: [FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890).

#### Scenario: A plugin calls with its own session

- **WHEN** Roam or Obsidian calls the route with the session it signed in with, and with no website cookie
- **THEN** the route identifies the caller's account and writes the payload ([FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890))

#### Scenario: No valid session

- **WHEN** a request carries no valid session
- **THEN** the route refuses it and writes nothing ([FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890))

### Requirement: The route checks the request body before writing

The upsert route SHALL check that the request body conforms to the CrossApp types before it writes anything. Sources: [ENG-2005](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2005), [FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890).

#### Scenario: A body that doesn't conform

- **WHEN** the request body doesn't conform to the CrossApp types
- **THEN** the route refuses the request and writes nothing ([ENG-2005](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2005))
===== graph-writes =====
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

How Roam and Obsidian write their nodes to the shared database, so a node is never left half-written and the two Roam write paths store the same values.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: One write per node

Roam sync and Obsidian sync SHALL write each node's Concept and its Content in one database call, with the Content inside the Concept. Roam and Obsidian SHALL make no Content-only write. Sources: [ENG-1794](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794), [ENG-1823](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823), [ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824).

#### Scenario: The write fails

- **WHEN** the database call that writes a node fails
- **THEN** that call leaves neither the node's Concept nor its Content written ([ENG-1794](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794), [ENG-1823](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823), [ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824))

#### Scenario: No Content-only write

- **WHEN** Roam sync or Obsidian sync writes a node
- **THEN** it makes no separate call that writes only the node's Content ([ENG-1823](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823), [ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824))

#### Scenario: Re-embedding from Roam's settings

- **WHEN** the suggestive-rules setting in Roam re-embeds block nodes
- **THEN** it writes each node's Content inside the node's Concept, not in a Content-only call ([ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824))

#### Scenario: The upsert route doesn't exist yet

- **WHEN** the upsert route from [FEE-890](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-890) is not built
- **THEN** Roam sync and Obsidian sync still write each node in one call, directly to the database ([ENG-1823](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1823), [ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824), [ENG-2412](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2412))

### Requirement: Node type Content goes inside its schema Concept

Roam sync SHALL write a node type's Content inside the node type's schema Concept, in the same call. Sources: [ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824).

#### Scenario: A node type changes

- **WHEN** Roam sync writes a changed node type
- **THEN** it makes no separate call that writes only the node type's Content ([ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824))

### Requirement: Sync repairs half-written nodes

The first sync after a graph or vault loads SHALL write again, in full, every node that the database holds without its Concept or without its Content. No data migration is needed. Sources: [ENG-1794](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794), [ENG-1793](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1793), [ENG-1791](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1791).

#### Scenario: A node is missing its Concept

- **WHEN** the database holds a node's Content but not its Concept, and the first sync after load runs
- **THEN** that sync writes the node's Concept and Content again ([ENG-1794](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1794), [ENG-1793](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1793), [ENG-1791](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1791))

### Requirement: Roam sync and Roam publish store the same values

Roam sync and Roam publish SHALL convert a node to its database values through the same CrossApp conversion, so neither overwrites the other with different values for an unchanged node. Sources: [ENG-2165](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165), [ENG-1824](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1824), [ENG-2166](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2166).

#### Scenario: Publish, then sync, an unchanged node

- **WHEN** Roam publish writes a node whose Source, if it has one, is already in the space, and Roam sync later writes the same node without any change to it in Roam
- **THEN** no field of the stored Concept or Content changes ([ENG-2165](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165), [ENG-2166](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2166))

#### Scenario: Sync, then publish, an unchanged node

- **WHEN** Roam sync writes a node whose Source, if it has one, is already in the space, and Roam publish later writes the same node without any change to it in Roam
- **THEN** no field of the stored Concept or Content changes ([ENG-2165](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2165), [ENG-2166](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2166))

## Context

See `proposal.md` for why. The state of main (`0b5aec5f`) that shapes the decisions:

- Roam sync and Obsidian sync write each node in two calls: Content with `upsert_content`, then the Concept with `upsert_concepts`. If the second call fails, the node is half-written. [ENG-1794] counted 2,753 missing Concepts on 2026-05-24; nobody has measured since.
- Since [ENG-1793] and [ENG-1791] (2026-05-31), the first sync after a graph or vault loads writes such nodes again.
- `upsert_concepts` accepts each node's Content inside its Concept since [ENG-1822].
- Roam publish already writes once: it builds a `CrossAppNode`, converts it with the shared converter and makes one `upsert_concepts` call. Roam sync converts with its own functions, so the two Roam write paths can store different values for the same node. [ENG-2202] had to reconcile node schema metadata between them. A third Roam path, the suggestive-rules setting, re-embeds block nodes with a Content-only write (`DiscourseNodeSuggestiveRules.tsx`).
- Obsidian has one write path for Concepts and Content: its publish writes access rows and asset files, but no Concept or Content. Obsidian doesn't use the CrossApp types.
- Roam relations already go through the CrossApp types: Roam publish writes them, and Roam discovery and import read them. Node discovery is the one read path that still returns its own type, `SharedNode`.
- Both plugins sign in to Supabase themselves. The only plugin call to the website that touches Supabase today creates a space before sign-in.
- Michael set a rule on 2026-07-17: callers reach the upsert route through an action-specific function, such as publish or sync, that builds the payload.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Record one answer, or one owner, for every open decision in the milestone's tickets.
- Order the work so each ticket lands as a small PR that can be reviewed and tested on its own.

**Non-Goals:**

- Designing the upsert route's open details. They stay open for Michael.
- Background polling for relations. The project excludes it from MVP0.
- Moving Linear tickets between milestones. That waits until Michael and Marc-Antoine have seen the decisions.

## Decisions

Each entry gives the question and the answer, the options on record with who proposed them and when, and the reason. When no option is on record, the entry says so. "Sid" answers were given in the decision review of 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22. "Confirmed" means a proposal from that review that Sid confirmed on 2026-10-22.

#### Does the route accept the plugin's own login? ([FEE-890])

- **Answer:** Yes. It's a requirement of [FEE-890], not a new ticket. (Confirmed)
- **Options on record:** None. PR #1237 (Marc-Antoine, 2026-07-18) reads the session from website cookies, which a plugin request doesn't carry; from reading the code, every plugin call would be refused with 401. This came up in the 2026-10-22 review.
- **Reason:** Without it, neither plugin can use the route, whatever its other details are. How the route reads the login stays open with the route's other details.

#### A request is missing a relation type: reject it, or look it up? ([FEE-890], [FEE-891])

- **Answer:** Open, needs Michael. It can wait until [ENG-1986]. (Confirmed)
- **Options on record:** Look it up in the database (PR #1237, Marc-Antoine, 2026-07-18). Reject the incomplete payload, because action functions build complete payloads (Michael, PR #1237 review, 2026-07-19).
- **Reason it can wait:** On main, only a relation triple schema that names its relation type by id needs it, and nothing sends that form: the one caller, Roam publish, passes no relation type, and Obsidian doesn't use the CrossApp types. It arrives with [ENG-1986]. If the route rejects, [FEE-891] adds a rejection case.
- **Linked:** what `upsert_concepts` does with a node schema it can't resolve, carried over from [ENG-2166], which says to decide the two together. Options on record: refuse the node (Marc-Antoine's asset-references spec, as cited in [ENG-2166]), or keep the stored schema (PR #1334, Marc-Antoine, 2026-08-23). From reading `concept.sql`, main stores the node with no schema and no error; not run.

#### What is the route called? ([FEE-890])

- **Answer:** Open, needs Michael.
- **Options on record:** `/api/internal/space/[id]` (PR #1237, Marc-Antoine, 2026-07-18). `/api/internal/space/[id]/graph/upsert`, or `/graph` if a GET comes later (Michael, 2026-07-19). `/api/internal/upsert` (Marc-Antoine, 2026-07-16). `/api/data/[space_id]` with POST and PATCH (Marc-Antoine, 2026-07-07).

#### When the route fails, what can a user do with the error? ([FEE-890])

- **Answer:** Open, needs Michael.
- **Options on record:** None. Michael asked on 2026-07-19 ("as a user, when I receive this message, what should I do with it?").
- **Context:** `upsert_concepts` returns one id per row: -1 for a name conflict, -2 for any other error. Roam sync throws with a count per code, Roam publish matches failures to its rows, Obsidian sync ignores the ids, and PR #1237 returns the database result as-is.

#### Who computes embeddings? ([FEE-890])

- **Answer:** Open, needs Michael.
- **Options on record:** None. [FEE-890] asks whether "all aspects of upserting" include embeddings.
- **Context:** Today each plugin gets vectors from the website and sends them inline; the CrossApp contract allows that. Estimate, not measured: a vector is about 20 KB as JSON, so a Roam batch of 200 nodes carries about 4 MB of vectors, close to the 4.5 MB request limit of a Vercel function, before [ENG-1824] adds full content. Either way, batch size becomes part of the route's design.

- **Answer:** Open, needs Michael.
- **Options on record:** PR #1238 (Marc-Antoine, 2026-07-19) starts Next for the whole database suite and waits for its "Ready in" output. Michael (review, 2026-07-20) asked to run only the route's feature in its own job and to wait with an HTTP health check.

#### What does discovery return? ([ENG-2091])

- **Answer:** `CrossAppNode`, with the missing fields added; `SharedNode` is removed. The ticket's Solution and Done When settle it.
- **Options on record:** `CrossAppNode` (Michael, 2026-07-22: "eventually should be CrossAppNode contract"; Marc-Antoine's Solution, 2026-08-03). Keep `SharedNode` as a lightweight listing (Sid, 2026-07-20). A listing type that wraps a `CrossAppNode` (the ticket's example), and a separate lookup of spaces (raised in the 2026-10-22 review); both dropped because they keep `SharedNode` under another shape.
- **Reason:** It's the ticket's plan and the team's direction. Sid's point about a light listing still holds: `content.full` is optional, and import fetches full content on its own.

#### Which fields does CrossAppNode gain? ([ENG-2091])

- **Answer:** Every field that a caller reads from the listing today, as the ticket's Solution says ("Add the missing fields to CrossAppNodes"). The list Sid confirmed on 2026-10-22 missed three of them; a review of this change found them the same day.

  - Missed: `spaceUri`. Roam shows and filters on it, and Roam import uses it. `rid` carries it, but `rid` is optional.
  - Missed: the node type's database id. Roam resolves node types by it (`resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`). `nodeType` holds the schema's local id.
  - Missed: the author's database account id. Obsidian's import modal shows author names from it. `CrossAppBase.authorId` holds the author's local id.
  - The other `SharedNode` fields already exist in another form: `localId`, `content.direct.value`, the dates and `slots`.
  - `modifiedAt` must stay the latest time of the Concept, the direct Content and the full Content, as `SharedNode.lastModified` is today. Otherwise refresh and the discover dialog's Modified column miss edits to a node's body.
- **Open, needs Marc-Antoine:** for the three missed fields, add each one to `CrossAppNode`, or change its caller to use the CrossApp form (a required `rid`, node types resolved by local id, author names looked up by local id).
- **Reason:** [ENG-2091]'s Done When is "We have removed SharedNodes without loss of functionality".

#### What did "sourceId" mean? ([ENG-2091])

- **Answer:** "Equivalent to sourceLocalId", as [ENG-2091] now records under that question. `sourceLocalId` already maps to `localId`, so there's nothing to add.

#### Which ticket builds the database-to-CrossAppNode converter for nodes? ([ENG-2091], [ENG-1985])

- **Answer:** [ENG-1985]. Its Done When covers all schemas, and only nodes are missing from `dbToCrossAppConverters.ts`. [ENG-2091] uses it. (Confirmed)

#### Does ENG-2045 wait for ENG-2091? ([ENG-2045])

- **Answer:** It follows [ENG-2091]. Its Done When already allows "the agreed cross-app return type".

#### How does Obsidian find relations made elsewhere between its own nodes? ([ENG-2394])

- **Answer:** The way Roam does: on every import and every refresh. (Sid, 2026-10-22)
- **Options on record:** Refresh-all, a dedicated check, or another explicitly scoped trigger ([ENG-2394], Michael, 2026-10-13). Background polling stays undecided, because the project excludes it from MVP0.
- **Reason:** No new command to learn, the two apps behave the same, and Obsidian already skips relations it holds.
- **Details (Confirmed):** in Obsidian, the lookup runs once per refresh, even when nothing is imported; a notice says how many relations were imported; the smallest change adds the vault's own published nodes to the existing "relations that reference these nodes" query. This is [ENG-2427].
- **Reproduction, from reading the code:** once user A has imported anything, Roam's lookup covers every visible relation, while Obsidian's covers only the spaces of the nodes in that import. So Obsidian misses the relation whenever user A has imported nothing from user B's space. Roam misses it only when user A has imported nothing at all: its refresh returns before the relation lookup when no imported node was refreshed (`refreshAllImportedNodes.ts:34`). Michael can confirm that the 2026-10-08 report matches.
- **Open, needs Michael:** whether refresh-all checks for relations when the user has no imported nodes, in both apps. Asked in [ENG-2428] (Product Decisions), with a proposed default of yes.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Roam sync and publish keep two conversions until [ENG-2165] lands] → [ENG-2202]'s parity test stays; [ENG-2166] stays in Icebox until then.
- [Obsidian's single write uses today's converters and gets reworked by [ENG-1986]] → Accepted; [ENG-1823] is small.
- [Inline vectors may push a route request past the platform's size limit] → Settled in the embeddings decision for [FEE-890]; batch size is part of the route's design.
- [Moving Roam publish onto the route adds a dependency on the website] → Weighed in the follow-up tickets after [FEE-890].
- [A space nobody opens keeps half-written nodes] → Accepted; no migration.
- [Obsidian's wider relation lookup adds a query to each refresh] → The smallest change extends an existing query.
- [Obsidian sync checks only the call's error, not the per-row ids that `upsert_concepts` returns, so after the single write a failed node is dropped without notice] → [ENG-1823] should check the row ids, as Roam sync does. No ticket says so yet.

- [Roam publish leaves out a node's Source slot when the Source isn't in the space yet, so publish and sync can still disagree on that slot after [ENG-2165]] → Accepted; the next sync writes the slot back.
